# Epic: `chat` — public real-time channels (biff's fourth modality)

## Why

biff's communication primitives map to a clean 2×2 — public/private × posted/real-time:

| | posted (async) | real-time |
|---------|----------------|-----------|
| **public** | wall | **chat — missing** |
| **private** | write | talk |

Three cells are filled: `wall` (public broadcast), `write` (private message),
`talk` (private 1:1 real-time). The public + real-time cell is empty. Every
multi-party collaboration mode we care about — a design debate among a leader
and specialists, a human overseeing and directing a swarm, a cross-repo
standup — has nowhere to live, because biff has no *place* where more than two
identities can talk in real time. `chat` fills that cell.

## The primitive

The other three modalities address a *person*. `chat` addresses a *place*: a
named channel (`#relay-refactor`) that exists on its own, that any team member
can walk into, and that outlives any single conversation held in it. That
"named place that persists" is the new primitive; IRC is its era-appropriate
name.

## Product requirements (outcomes)

1. **A channel is a named, persistent place.** It exists whether or not anyone
   is currently in it. Team members can list channels, join, and leave.
2. **Participants are identities — agent or human, indistinguishable.** No
   "bots are second-class." `rmh` and `jim` are the same kind of occupant: both
   join, speak, read, and part with the same permissions vocabulary. Consistent
   with how `wall`/`write`/`talk` already treat agents and people identically.
3. **Public within the team.** A channel is visible and joinable by the team,
   unlike `write`/`talk`, which are private to their two parties. `chat` is the
   public half of real-time, as `wall` is the public half of posted.
4. **Real-time delivery plus backlog on join.** Occupants see messages live;
   joining shows recent history so you land in context, not a blank room.
5. **Direction, not just observation.** A human in a channel can steer the
   agents present — ask for status, redirect work — and agents act on it.
   Steering stays governed by biff's existing human-in-the-loop consent model:
   an agent acts because it chose to read and honor a directive, never because
   something was pushed into its process.
6. **Interop from standard IRC clients.** A human joins channels from any
   ordinary IRC client — irssi, weechat, a phone app — and participates as a
   first-class occupant. Oversight and direction of a swarm work from anywhere,
   with no new UI to build or learn.
7. **Durable, auditable history.** Channel transcripts are retained and
   retrievable, so a channel doubles as an audit trail of how a piece of work
   was coordinated — who said what, when — and can feed the org's knowledge
   base.
8. **Self-hostable and locked down for corporate / small teams.** The
   deployment runs privately: authenticated accounts required to connect,
   encrypted transport, admin-controlled membership, and no connection to
   public IRC networks. A small team can stand it up and trust it out of the
   box.

## End-user experience

Command vocabulary extends the existing biff set (`wall`/`write`/`talk`), so it
feels native:

- `/join #relay-refactor` — enter a channel (creating it if new, per policy).
- messaging in-channel — speak to everyone present.
- `/who #relay-refactor` — see who is in the room (agents and humans together).
- `/part` — leave.
- channel topic — a one-line "what this room is for."

A human running an ordinary IRC client sees the same channels and the same
occupants; an agent sees them through biff's tools. Same room, two front doors.

## Basic technical dependencies (not implementation)

- Rides the same self-hostable deployment as the NATS relay (see the NATS
  docker image bead).
- Bundles a reasonable, locked-down open-source IRC daemon. **Ergo** is the
  leading candidate: single binary, built-in accounts and SASL, TLS, native
  message history, no federation. Runs as a second service alongside NATS.

## Non-goals (what `chat` is NOT)

Consistent with biff's "purposeful, not chatty" thesis:

- No threads, reactions, emoji, or file uploads. This is not Slack.
- No public or federated IRC networks — private, org-scoped only.
- biff itself does not become a general chat archive; durable history is a
  capture concern, not a new biff data store.

## Product decisions this epic surfaces (need a ruling)

- **prfaq amendment.** The prfaq currently lists "no channels" under what we are
  not building. Channels as a deliberate fourth modality reverses that; the
  prfaq and design log need updating before build.
- **How much persistence.** Whether history lives only for backlog/audit vs.
  becomes searchable org knowledge — and whether that ties into the Ask Your Org
  enterprise-search "Chat connector" opportunity.

## Acceptance (outcome-level)

- A human and two or more agents hold a live, coherent design discussion in a
  shared channel, with the human joining from a standard IRC client.
- A human issues a directive in-channel and an agent acts on it under the
  consent model.
- A channel's history is retrievable after the fact as an audit record of the
  work.

tool_input.content:
# Epic: `chat` — public real-time channels (biff's fourth modality)

## The job (why this exists)

A lead running a swarm of agents needs to **watch and redirect them in one
place** — without tabbing between six Claude sessions or serializing everything
through 1:1 `write`s. Two concrete jobs:

1. **Oversee** — see what a group of agents (and humans) are saying to each
   other as work happens, in one shared place.
2. **Direct** — inject direction into that place and have agents act on it, with
   the same human-in-the-loop consent biff already requires for steering.

Today biff has no *place* where more than two identities talk in real time, so
both jobs are homeless. `chat` is that place.

> Illustration, not the argument: biff's primitives form a 2×2 —
> `wall` (public/posted), `write` (private/posted), `talk` (private/real-time).
> `chat` is the empty public/real-time cell. The grid explains the *shape*; the
> job above is the *reason*.

**Discovery owed before build:** 3–5 interviews (with `tdt`) with people running
agent swarms, to confirm the director job is real and not just tidy taxonomy.

## The primitive

The other three modalities address an *identity* — a named participant, agent or
human, no distinction. `chat` addresses a *place*: a named channel
(`#relay-refactor`) that exists on its own, that any participant can walk into,
and that outlives any conversation held in it. IRC is its era-appropriate name.

## Two phases (one epic)

Ships as two phases so the low-risk value lands first and the hard security work
is isolated:

- **Phase A — the channel primitive.** A public place: create/list, join/part,
  live delivery + backlog, durable transcript, participation from standard IRC
  clients. Delivers the *oversee* job on its own.
- **Phase B — consented steering (depends on A).** A participant directs agents
  in-channel; agents act only on authenticated, consented directives. Delivers
  the *direct* job. Carries its own security design.

## Product requirements (outcomes)

### Phase A

1. **A channel is a named, persistent place** — exists whether or not anyone is
   in it; participants can list, join, and leave.
2. **Participants are identities, agent or human, indistinguishable** — same
   join/speak/read/part, same permissions vocabulary. No "bots are
   second-class."
3. **Public within the team** — visible and joinable, unlike `write`/`talk`.
4. **Live delivery plus backlog on join** — occupants land in context, not a
   blank room. (See the attention-model spike: "live" for an agent is bounded
   by its notification cadence.)
5. **A participant can join and speak from outside a Claude session** — from an
   ordinary client, no biff-specific app to install. *(Implementation: standard
   IRC clients against a private IRCd — see dependencies.)*
6. **Durable, auditable transcript** — retrievable after the fact as a record
   of how work was coordinated (who said what, when).

### Phase B

7. **A participant can direct agents in-channel and they act on it** — under
   consent, never pushed into an agent's process.
8. **Directives are cryptographically authenticated** — an agent honors a
   directive only if it is GPG-signed and verifies against a trusted key for
   that identity, independent of the transport nick. Adopt beadle's proven
   four-level trust model (trusted / verified / untrusted / unverified, keyed on
   `gpg --verify`; beadle DES-001). This is the answer to "how does an IRC nick
   prove it is `jim`" — the signature proves it, not the nick.
9. **N:M consent is explicit** — in a room of many humans and agents, each agent
   has a defined policy for *whose* directives it will act on (e.g. designated
   lead(s) only), not "anyone present."

## End-user experience

Vocabulary extends the existing set (`wall`/`write`/`talk`), so it feels native:

- `/join #relay-refactor` — enter a channel (create if new, per policy).
- `/say #relay-refactor <msg>` — **speak in the room** (the primary action;
  `wall` is team-broadcast and `write` is 1:1, so channel speech needs its own
  verb).
- `/who #relay-refactor` — channel roster (agents and humans together).
- `/part #relay-refactor` — leave.
- channel topic — a one-line "what this room is for."

A human on an ordinary IRC client and an agent via biff tools see the same room
and the same occupants: same room, two front doors. An explicit **IRC-nick ↔
biff-identity resolution** is required so the two doors open onto the same
person.

## Attention model (make-or-break — resolved by the spike)

A public real-time room is a monitoring surface, and biff exists to *kill*
monitoring surfaces ("no channels to monitor"). So channels must be
**read-on-demand / opt-in-notify**, governed by `/mesg` — joining a channel must
not turn into a live ping on every message. And for agents, "real-time" is
really **poll-time**: today agents only see traffic on their next tool call via
mutated tool descriptions + `tools/list_changed` (DESIGN.md DES-004/020/036).
Channel chat works *well* only if push-into-prompt works — see the spike.

## Spikes / open decisions (gate the build)

- **SPIKE — Claude Code Channels.** Prove `notifications/claude/channel`
  (DES-036/DES-042) can push channel traffic directly into an agent's prompt
  queue at usable latency. This is the mechanism the whole modality rides on; if
  it doesn't work for agents, `chat` degrades to poll-time and the *direct* job
  is unusable. **Everything downstream depends on this spike.**
- **Discovery** — the swarm-director interviews above.
- **prfaq amendment (explicit reversals).** This epic reverses *four* stated
  commitments; the prfaq and design log must be updated and the CEO must rule
  before build:
  1. "No channels" — reversed by the whole epic.
  2. "No message history / not a system of record" — reversed by req 6.
  3. "No mobile app" — a phone IRC client is now in the target workflow.
  4. **E2E privacy.** biff's headline guarantee is that the relay never sees
     message contents. A standard IRC client requires the IRCd to see plaintext.
     **Ruling (operator, this session): channel messages are E2E-EXEMPT** —
     plaintext to relay/IRCd is accepted, and `chat` must be *labeled* as
     not-E2E so users know DMs (`write`/`talk`) and channels differ.
- **How much persistence** — retention window, which command reads history, and
  whether the transcript feeds the Ask-Your-Org enterprise-search "Chat
  connector" opportunity or stays audit-only.

## Basic technical dependencies (not implementation)

- Rides the same self-hostable deployment as the NATS relay (see the NATS docker
  image bead).
- Bundles a locked-down open-source IRC daemon — **Ergo** candidate: single
  binary, built-in accounts + SASL, TLS, native message history, no federation.
  Runs as a second service alongside NATS.
- Phase B trust reuses beadle's GPG verification model (`gpg --verify`,
  four-level trust). Threat-model review by `djb`/`bcs` required.

## Non-goals (what `chat` is NOT)

Consistent with "purposeful, not chatty":

- No threads, reactions, emoji, or file uploads. This is not Slack.
- No public or federated IRC networks — private, org-scoped only.
- No cross-channel/cross-team federation.
- No message editing/deletion/moderation tooling.
- `chat` does not replace `write`/`talk` — use `write`/`talk` for private 1:1;
  `chat` for a public room.

## Acceptance (outcome-level)

- **Phase A:** a human (from a standard IRC client) and two or more agents hold
  a live, coherent design discussion in a shared channel; a newcomer joining
  sees backlog and lands in context; the transcript is retrievable afterward as
  an audit record.
- **Phase B:** a human issues a GPG-signed directive in-channel; a target agent
  verifies it against a trusted key and acts; an unsigned or untrusted directive
  is not acted on.

tool_input.content:
# Spike: prove Claude Code Channels can drive real-time chat for agents

**Parent:** biff-6gk (chat — public real-time channels)
**Type:** spike (investigation, timeboxed)

## Question

Can `notifications/claude/channel` (Claude Code Channels) push channel traffic
**directly into an agent's prompt queue** at usable latency — eliminating the
poll-time gap that today limits an agent to seeing traffic only on its next tool
call?

This is the mechanism the entire `chat` modality rides on. If it does not work
for agents, `chat` degrades to poll-time (tool-description mutation +
`tools/list_changed`, DESIGN.md DES-004/020/036), and Phase B (in-channel
direction of a swarm) is unusable. **Everything downstream of biff-6gk depends
on the answer.**

## Background

- Today biff has **no** MCP push that renders in Claude Code. Unread alerts are
  faked with dynamic tool descriptions + `tools/list_changed` + a status-line
  file (DES-004). Latency is 0–2s **only when a tool description changes**, and
  the model only notices on its **next turn**.
- DES-036/DES-042 identified Claude Code Channels
  (`notifications/claude/channel`) as a way for an MCP server to push content
  straight into Claude's prompt queue — no `/loop`, no polling, the push *is*
  the prompt. This has not been proven for biff.

## What to find out

1. **Does it render / drive action?** Does a `notifications/claude/channel`
   message actually reach a running Claude Code agent and cause it to act —
   versus being silently dropped (as `notifications/message` was; Claude Code
   issue #3174)?
2. **Latency.** End-to-end from "message posted in channel" to "agent has it in
   context." Target: comparable to human real-time (single-digit seconds).
3. **Transport constraints.** Does it require SSE/HTTP, or does it work over
   stdio? What must the MCP server hold (session reference, connection) to send
   it? (Cross-reference the belt/suspenders session-capture problem, DES-004.)
4. **Rate / coalescing.** Behavior under channel traffic — many messages in a
   short window. Does it flood the prompt queue? Is coalescing needed (cf. the
   talk queue bound, DES-044)?
5. **Attention control.** Can delivery be gated (opt-in-notify per `/mesg`) so a
   joined channel is not a firehose into every occupant's prompt?

## Deliverable

A short findings doc (`.md`) with a **go / no-go / conditional** recommendation
for the `chat` modality, covering each question above with measured evidence
(not assertion — per "any property not verified does not exist"). If the answer
is no-go, state the fallback (poll-time chat) and whether the *oversee* job
(Phase A) still stands without push.

## Non-goals

- No production implementation of `chat`. This is a feasibility probe.
- No IRCd / Ergo work — this spike is purely the agent-side delivery mechanism.

## Notes

- Likely needs a minimal MCP server emitting `notifications/claude/channel` and
  a real Claude Code session as the observer (SDK or subprocess tier).
- Confirm current Claude Code support for the notification — the DES-036/042
  entries are a design intent, not a verified capability.

# Spike: prove Claude Code Channels can push directly into an agent's prompt

**Blocks:** biff-6gk (chat — public real-time channels)
**Type:** spike (investigation, timeboxed)

## Why this is foundational (not chat-specific)

Claude Code Channels (`notifications/claude/channel`) push content **directly
into a running agent's prompt queue** — no `/loop`, no polling, the push *is*
the prompt. That attacks the single recurring limitation across biff: agents
only notice anything on their **next tool call**. The poll-time gap has been
patched repeatedly and never eliminated:

- **talk** push notifications (DES-020/021) — the whole
  tool-description-mutation + `tools/list_changed` dance exists to work around
  the absence of push.
- **mail / unread** delivery (DES-036) — two-layer polling + auto-poll-on-write,
  all to approximate a push.
- **presence / wall** (DES-004) — status-line file polling, 0–2s only when a
  description changes.

If Channels work, they collapse all of that machinery and unlock genuine
real-time for **every** biff modality — and they are the mechanism the `chat`
epic (biff-6gk) rides on. So this spike is worth running on its own merits; the
chat epic is one beneficiary, not the reason.

## Question

Can `notifications/claude/channel` push a message **directly into an agent's
prompt queue** at usable latency, versus the current poll-time model
(tool-description mutation + `tools/list_changed`, DESIGN.md DES-004/020/036)?

tool_input.content:
# Spike scope — Claude Code Channels test harness (biff-qlz)

## Goal

Prove, with measured evidence, that biff's stdio MCP server can emit
`notifications/claude/channel` into a live Claude Code session, and characterize
latency / coalescing / consent — **without removing the current poll-time
delivery**. Feasibility + characterization only. No production adoption.

## Hard constraint — dual support

Channels is an **opt-in second emitter**, not a replacement:

- The existing path stays intact: tool-description mutation + `tools/list_changed`
  + status-line file (DES-004/020/036). When Channels is off or the session was
  launched without `--channels`, biff behaves **exactly as today**.
- Channels fires only when (a) the session enabled it and (b) a biff config flag
  opts in. Both emitters may run at once; the spike must confirm they don't
  conflict (no double-surfacing, no regression to today's path).
- `biff-5esx` ("replace both polling layers when stable") stays future. This
  spike does not touch the two-layer machinery.

## Harness (minimal)

1. **Emitter:** a `biff serve` mode (or a stripped fork of it) that declares
   `capabilities.experimental['claude/channel'] = {}` and, on relay message
   arrival, *also* emits `notifications/claude/channel {content, meta}` —
   reusing the same `refresh_*` hook that fires today's description update.
2. **Session:** `claude --dangerously-load-development-channels server:biff`
   (`channelsEnabled` already on for punt-labs; dev flag bypasses the allowlist).
3. **Trigger:** a second identity sends `/wall`, `/write`, `/talk` through the
   relay → observe whether a `<channel source="biff" …>` tag lands in the
   session and the model reacts.
4. **Driver:** an **interactive** session is required — SDK (Tier 4) and raw
   stdio (Tier 3) do NOT receive channel events. Automate via tmux +
   `capture-pane`, reusing the DES-023 status-line E2E harness pattern.

## Measurements (write expected output first, then compare)

| Question | Method | Pass bar |
|---|---|---|
| **FastMCP feasibility** (gating — do FIRST) | Declare experimental cap + emit custom notification from Python FastMCP | Event reaches the session at all |
| Does it render + drive action | Inspect pane for `← biff: …`; confirm model acts | yes |
| Latency, idle agent | relay-send → in-context timestamp | single-digit seconds |
| Latency, busy agent | send mid-task | delivered at next turn boundary (per docs) |
| Coalescing | N rapid sends | grouped, count events, no flood |
| Graceful when off | close session / flag off | no crash; today's path still delivers |
| No regression | run with Channels on | existing description/status-line path unchanged |

## Stretch (only if base passes)

- **Permission relay round-trip** (`…/permission_request` + `…/permission`) as
  the Phase-B remote-consent probe for `biff-6gk`.

## Out of scope

IRCd/Ergo, chat channels, removal of polling, production allowlist change, org
rollout, remote transport.

## Deliverable

A findings `.md`: **go / no-go** on Channels-as-additive-emitter, the measured
latency table, the **FastMCP verdict** (if Python can't emit the notification,
that's a hard blocker — stop and report), per-modality impact (wall/write/talk),
and whether permission relay is viable for Phase B.

"""Standalone minimal Claude Code Channels emitter — the gating feasibility probe.

Answers one question with evidence: can a Python FastMCP stdio server (a)
advertise ``capabilities.experimental['claude/channel'] = {}`` in its
``initialize`` result and (b) emit a custom ``notifications/claude/channel``
notification over stdio?

Run directly as an MCP stdio server:

    uv run python -m spikes.channels.emitter

Two escape hatches make this work, neither of which touches biff's production
source:

1. ``FastMCP.run_stdio_async`` hardcodes ``create_initialization_options``
   without experimental capabilities, so this module drives the low-level
   ``Server.run`` itself with ``experimental_capabilities`` injected.
2. ``Context.send_notification`` wraps the notification in ``ServerNotification``
   (a closed union that rejects unknown methods).  Bypass it by calling
   ``ctx.session.send_notification`` directly with a generic
   ``Notification[dict, str]`` — the base ``ServerSession`` serializes whatever
   it is handed via ``model_dump`` with no union validation.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

import mcp.types as mcp_types
from fastmcp import Context, FastMCP
from fastmcp.server.dependencies import get_context
from mcp.server.lowlevel.server import NotificationOptions
from mcp.server.stdio import stdio_server

CHANNEL_CAPABILITY: str = "claude/channel"
CHANNEL_METHOD: str = "notifications/claude/channel"

app: FastMCP[None] = FastMCP("biff-channels-spike")


def channel_notification(content: str, source: str) -> mcp_types.Notification[dict[str, Any], str]:
    """Build a raw ``notifications/claude/channel`` notification.

    The generic ``Notification[dict, str]`` accepts an arbitrary method string,
    unlike the concrete server-notification classes whose method is a ``Literal``.
    """
    return mcp_types.Notification[dict[str, Any], str](
        method=CHANNEL_METHOD,
        params={"content": content, "meta": {"source": source}},
    )


@app.tool
async def emit_channel(content: str, source: str = "biff") -> str:
    """Emit one channel notification and confirm what was sent."""
    ctx: Context[Any, Any, Any] = get_context()
    await ctx.session.send_notification(channel_notification(content, source))
    return f"emitted channel: {content!r} (source={source})"


async def _serve() -> None:
    """Run over stdio with the experimental channel capability advertised."""
    server = app._mcp_server  # noqa: SLF001 — spike drives the low-level run directly
    async with app._lifespan_manager():  # noqa: SLF001
        async with stdio_server() as (read_stream, write_stream):
            await server.run(
                read_stream,
                write_stream,
                server.create_initialization_options(
                    notification_options=NotificationOptions(tools_changed=True),
                    experimental_capabilities={CHANNEL_CAPABILITY: {}},
                ),
            )


def main() -> None:
    """Entry point for ``python -m spikes.channels.emitter``."""
    import anyio

    anyio.run(_serve)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Raw-stdio gate probe — proves the channel emitter on the wire.

Spawns :mod:`spikes.channels.emitter` as a subprocess, speaks the MCP
JSON-RPC handshake by hand, calls the ``emit_channel`` tool, and reads every
line the server writes back.  Nothing here uses a validating MCP client: the
point is to observe the exact bytes Claude Code would see, so a client that
silently drops unknown notifications cannot mask the result.

Two assertions settle the gating question:

1. The ``initialize`` result advertises
   ``capabilities.experimental['claude/channel']``.
2. A ``notifications/claude/channel`` JSON-RPC notification reaches stdout with
   the expected ``params.content``.

Exit 0 and print ``GATE: PASS`` when both hold; exit 1 with the captured lines
otherwise.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from typing import Any

CHANNEL_METHOD = "notifications/claude/channel"
NEEDLE = "gate-probe-needle"


def _send(proc: subprocess.Popen[str], message: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    """Write one newline-delimited JSON-RPC message to the server's stdin."""
    assert proc.stdin is not None
    proc.stdin.write(json.dumps(message) + "\n")
    proc.stdin.flush()


def _read_json_lines(proc: subprocess.Popen[str], count: int, timeout: float) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Read up to *count* JSON messages from stdout within *timeout* seconds."""
    assert proc.stdout is not None
    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
    messages: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    while len(messages) < count and time.monotonic() < deadline:
        line = proc.stdout.readline()
        if not line:
            break
        line = line.strip()
        if not line:
            continue
        messages.append(json.loads(line))
    return messages


def run_probe() -> tuple[bool, list[dict[str, Any]]]:
    """Drive the emitter over stdio and return ``(passed, captured_messages)``."""
    proc = subprocess.Popen(
        [sys.executable, "-m", "spikes.channels.emitter"],
        stdin=subprocess.PIPE,
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
        text=True,
    )
    try:
        _send(
            proc,
            {
                "jsonrpc": "2.0",
                "id": 1,
                "method": "initialize",
                "params": {
                    "protocolVersion": "2025-06-18",
                    "capabilities": {},
                    "clientInfo": {"name": "gate-probe", "version": "0"},
                },
            },
        )
        init_result = _read_json_lines(proc, count=1, timeout=10.0)
        _send(proc, {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": "notifications/initialized"})
        _send(
            proc,
            {
                "jsonrpc": "2.0",
                "id": 2,
                "method": "tools/call",
                "params": {"name": "emit_channel", "arguments": {"content": NEEDLE}},
            },
        )
        # The tool response and the channel notification arrive in either order.
        tail = _read_json_lines(proc, count=2, timeout=10.0)
    finally:
        proc.terminate()
        try:
            proc.wait(timeout=5.0)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            proc.kill()

    captured = init_result + tail
    experimental = (
        init_result[0].get("result", {}).get("capabilities", {}).get("experimental", {})
        if init_result
        else {}
    )
    cap_ok = "claude/channel" in experimental
    channel_msgs = [m for m in tail if m.get("method") == CHANNEL_METHOD]
    notif_ok = any(
        m.get("params", {}).get("content") == NEEDLE for m in channel_msgs
    )
    return cap_ok and notif_ok, captured


def main() -> int:
    """Run the probe, print a verdict with evidence, and return an exit code."""
    passed, captured = run_probe()
    print("=== captured JSON-RPC messages ===")
    for msg in captured:
        print(json.dumps(msg))
    print("=== verdict ===")
    print("GATE: PASS" if passed else "GATE: FAIL")
    return 0 if passed else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

"""Opt-in Claude Code Channels emitter — a second, additive delivery path.

Claude Code's Channels research preview lets an MCP server push a
``notifications/claude/channel`` message into a live interactive session, where
it surfaces as a ``<channel>`` tag the model reads on its next turn.  Biff's
existing delivery (tool-description mutation + ``tools/list_changed`` +
status-line file) is unchanged; this module fires *in addition* when opted in,
never instead.

The emitter is gated on the ``BIFF_CHANNELS`` environment variable so it is off
by default.  When off, :func:`emit_channel` is a no-op and
:func:`channel_experimental_capabilities` returns an empty map, so the server
advertises and behaves exactly as it does today.

Two escape hatches make custom-method notifications work over FastMCP:

* the server must advertise ``capabilities.experimental['claude/channel']`` —
  injected via :func:`channel_experimental_capabilities`;
* ``Context.send_notification`` wraps its argument in ``ServerNotification`` (a
  closed union that rejects unknown methods), so :func:`emit_channel` sends the
  raw notification directly on the ``ServerSession`` instead, whose base
  ``send_notification`` serializes whatever it is handed.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import os
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, cast

import mcp.types as mcp_types

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from mcp.server.session import ServerSession

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

CHANNEL_CAPABILITY = "claude/channel"
CHANNEL_METHOD = "notifications/claude/channel"
_ENABLE_ENV = "BIFF_CHANNELS"
_TRUTHY = frozenset({"1", "true", "yes", "on"})

ChannelNotification = mcp_types.Notification[dict[str, Any], str]


def channels_enabled() -> bool:
    """Return whether the opt-in channel emitter is turned on."""
    return os.environ.get(_ENABLE_ENV, "").strip().lower() in _TRUTHY


def channel_experimental_capabilities() -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
    """Return the experimental capability map to advertise (empty when off)."""
    return {CHANNEL_CAPABILITY: {}} if channels_enabled() else {}


async def emit_channel(
    session: ServerSession, content: str, *, source: str = "biff"
) -> None:
    """Emit one ``notifications/claude/channel`` on *session*, best-effort.

    No-op when channels are disabled.  Delivery failures are logged, never
    raised — a dead session must not break the caller, matching the belt/
    suspenders contract of :func:`notify_tool_list_changed`.
    """
    if not channels_enabled():
        return
    notification = ChannelNotification(
        method=CHANNEL_METHOD,
        params={"content": content, "meta": {"source": source}},
    )
    try:
        # The base ServerSession.send_notification only calls model_dump on its
        # argument, so a raw Notification rides through untouched; the cast
        # satisfies the ServerNotification-typed signature (PY-TS-12).
        await session.send_notification(
            cast("mcp_types.ServerNotification", notification)
        )
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — best-effort, mirrors notify_tool_list_changed
        logger.warning("Failed to send channel notification", exc_info=True)

async def notify_tool_list_changed(*, channel_content: str | None = None) -> None:
    """Fire ``notifications/tools/list_changed`` via the best available path.

    Belt path (inside a tool handler): queues the notification on the
    FastMCP Context so it piggybacks on the tool response.

    Suspenders path (background poller): sends directly on the stored
    ServerSession when no request context is active.

    When *channel_content* is given and the opt-in Channels emitter is enabled
    (``BIFF_CHANNELS``), also pushes a ``notifications/claude/channel`` carrying
    that summary on the *same* session — an additive second delivery that
    reuses this single hook rather than a parallel path.  With Channels off
    (the default) the extra emit is a no-op and behavior is exactly as today.
    """
    global _session

    from biff.server.channels import emit_channel  # noqa: PLC0415

    # Belt path — inside a tool handler, Context is available.
    try:
        from fastmcp.server.dependencies import get_context  # noqa: PLC0415
        from mcp.types import ToolListChangedNotification  # noqa: PLC0415

        ctx = get_context()
        await ctx.send_notification(ToolListChangedNotification())
        # Always update — the client may have reconnected with a new session.
        _session = ctx.session
        if channel_content is not None:
            await emit_channel(ctx.session, channel_content)
        return
    except RuntimeError:
        pass

    # Suspenders path — no request context, use stored session.
    # Bare Exception matches FastMCP's own _flush_notifications pattern —
    # notification delivery is best-effort and must never crash the poller.
    if _session is not None:
        try:
            await _session.send_tool_list_changed()
            if channel_content is not None:
                await emit_channel(_session, channel_content)
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
            logger.warning(
                "Failed to send tool list changed notification",
                exc_info=True,
            )
            # Session is dead — clear it so the poller stops
            # hammering a closed stream every tick.
            _session = None

"""Tests for the opt-in Claude Code Channels emitter.

The hard constraint is dual-support: with ``BIFF_CHANNELS`` unset (the
default) the emitter is inert and biff's existing delivery is untouched; with
it set, a channel notification fires *in addition* to the tool-description
path, carrying the same arrival summary exactly once (no double-surfacing).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
from unittest.mock import AsyncMock

import pytest

from biff.server import channels
from biff.server.channels import (
    CHANNEL_METHOD,
    channel_experimental_capabilities,
    channels_enabled,
    emit_channel,
)
from biff.server.tools import _descriptions

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from collections.abc import Iterator


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def _clean_channel_env(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> Iterator[None]:
    """Ensure each test starts with the channels flag unset."""
    monkeypatch.delenv("BIFF_CHANNELS", raising=False)
    yield
    _descriptions._reset_session()


class TestChannelsFlag:
    def test_disabled_by_default(self) -> None:
        assert channels_enabled() is False

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("value", ["1", "true", "TRUE", "yes", "on", " on "])
    def test_enabled_for_truthy_values(
        self, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, value: str
    ) -> None:
        monkeypatch.setenv("BIFF_CHANNELS", value)
        assert channels_enabled() is True

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("value", ["", "0", "false", "no", "off", "nope"])
    def test_disabled_for_falsy_values(
        self, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, value: str
    ) -> None:
        monkeypatch.setenv("BIFF_CHANNELS", value)
        assert channels_enabled() is False


class TestExperimentalCapabilities:
    def test_empty_when_disabled(self) -> None:
        assert channel_experimental_capabilities() == {}

    def test_advertises_when_enabled(self, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
        monkeypatch.setenv("BIFF_CHANNELS", "1")
        assert channel_experimental_capabilities() == {"claude/channel": {}}


class TestEmitChannel:
    async def test_noop_when_disabled(self) -> None:
        session = AsyncMock()
        await emit_channel(session, "you have 1 unread")
        session.send_notification.assert_not_called()

    async def test_emits_raw_notification_when_enabled(
        self, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
    ) -> None:
        monkeypatch.setenv("BIFF_CHANNELS", "1")
        session = AsyncMock()
        await emit_channel(session, "you have 1 unread", source="biff")
        session.send_notification.assert_awaited_once()
        sent = session.send_notification.await_args.args[0]
        dumped = sent.model_dump(by_alias=True, mode="json", exclude_none=True)
        assert dumped["method"] == CHANNEL_METHOD
        assert dumped["params"]["content"] == "you have 1 unread"
        assert dumped["params"]["meta"]["source"] == "biff"

    async def test_delivery_failure_is_swallowed(
        self, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
    ) -> None:
        monkeypatch.setenv("BIFF_CHANNELS", "1")
        session = AsyncMock()
        session.send_notification.side_effect = RuntimeError("dead stream")
        # Best-effort: a dead session must not raise into the caller.
        await emit_channel(session, "boom")


class TestNotifyHookDualSupport:
    """The suspenders path (background poller) drives both emitters."""

    async def test_channels_off_sends_only_list_changed(self) -> None:
        session = AsyncMock()
        _descriptions.capture_session(session)
        await _descriptions.notify_tool_list_changed(channel_content="2 unread")
        session.send_tool_list_changed.assert_awaited_once()
        session.send_notification.assert_not_called()

    async def test_channels_on_sends_both(
        self, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
    ) -> None:
        monkeypatch.setenv("BIFF_CHANNELS", "1")
        session = AsyncMock()
        _descriptions.capture_session(session)
        await _descriptions.notify_tool_list_changed(channel_content="2 unread")
        session.send_tool_list_changed.assert_awaited_once()
        session.send_notification.assert_awaited_once()

    async def test_no_channel_without_content_even_when_enabled(
        self, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
    ) -> None:
        monkeypatch.setenv("BIFF_CHANNELS", "1")
        session = AsyncMock()
        _descriptions.capture_session(session)
        # A description change with no arrival summary (e.g. a revert to base)
        # must not surface a channel.
        await _descriptions.notify_tool_list_changed()
        session.send_tool_list_changed.assert_awaited_once()
        session.send_notification.assert_not_called()

    async def test_content_surfaces_exactly_once(
        self, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
    ) -> None:
        monkeypatch.setenv("BIFF_CHANNELS", "1")
        session = AsyncMock()
        _descriptions.capture_session(session)
        await _descriptions.notify_tool_list_changed(channel_content="2 unread")
        assert channels.channels_enabled() is True
        # One list_changed, one channel — the same arrival is not double-sent.
        assert session.send_tool_list_changed.await_count == 1
        assert session.send_notification.await_count == 1

"""Runnable biff MCP server with the opt-in Channels emitter and capability.

Wraps biff's real :func:`biff.server.app.create_server` output and runs it over
stdio with ``experimental_capabilities['claude/channel']`` advertised —
something FastMCP's own ``run_stdio_async`` does not inject.  Point an
interactive Claude Code session at this module to exercise the additive channel
emitter end to end against the *real* relay, tools, and refresh hook.

    BIFF_CHANNELS=1 uv run python -m spikes.channels.serve

When ``BIFF_CHANNELS`` is unset the capability map is empty and the server
advertises exactly as production biff does — the dual-support default.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

import anyio
from mcp.server.lowlevel.server import NotificationOptions
from mcp.server.stdio import stdio_server

from biff.__main__ import _create_mcp_server
from biff.server.channels import channel_experimental_capabilities


async def _serve() -> None:
    """Build the real biff server and run stdio with channel caps injected."""
    server = _create_mcp_server(
        user=None,
        data_dir=None,
        relay_url=None,
        prefix=Path(tempfile.gettempdir()),
    )
    low = server._mcp_server
    async with (
        server._lifespan_manager(),
        stdio_server() as (read_stream, write_stream),
    ):
        await low.run(
            read_stream,
            write_stream,
            low.create_initialization_options(
                notification_options=NotificationOptions(tools_changed=True),
                experimental_capabilities=channel_experimental_capabilities(),
            ),
        )


def main() -> None:
    """Entry point for ``python -m spikes.channels.serve``."""
    anyio.run(_serve)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from pathlib import Path

# ``tests/conftest.py`` resets ``_descriptions`` globals autouse, and
# ``monkeypatch`` auto-restores ``BIFF_CHANNELS`` after each test.


def _channel_init_capabilities(tmp_path: Path) -> dict[str, dict[str, object]] | None:
    """Build the real biff server and return its advertised experimental caps.

    Mirrors what ``spikes/channels/serve.py`` does: create the production
    server via :func:`create_server` and inject the channel capability the same
    way, so the assertion reflects the real ``initialize`` result.
    """
    state = create_state(
        BiffConfig(user="kai", repo_name="_test-channels"),
        tmp_path,
        tty="tty1",
        hostname="test-host",
        pwd="/test",
    )
    server = create_server(state)
    opts = server._mcp_server.create_initialization_options(
        notification_options=NotificationOptions(tools_changed=True),
        experimental_capabilities=channel_experimental_capabilities(),
    )
    return opts.capabilities.experimental

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# harness.sh — interactive E2E harness for the Claude Code Channels spike.
#
# Proves whether biff's opt-in channel emitter surfaces a
# notifications/claude/channel event inside a LIVE interactive Claude Code
# session.  Channels are stdio-only AND interactive-session-only: the Agent SDK
# (Tier 4) and raw stdio (Tier 3) do NOT receive channel events, so this must
# drive a real `claude` TUI.  Automated via tmux + capture-pane, reusing the
# DES-023 status-line E2E pattern (scripts/test-talk-e2e.sh).
#
# Topology:
#   pane A — the RECEIVER: a real `claude` launched with
#            `--dangerously-load-development-channels server:biff-channels`,
#            pointed at spikes/channels/serve.py (real biff server + the
#            experimental claude/channel capability, BIFF_CHANNELS=1).
#   pane B — the SENDER: a plain shell that runs `biff wall <needle>` to push a
#            team broadcast through the relay into the receiver.
#
# Both clones are named "biff" (different parents) so they share one NATS
# namespace (DES-007: namespace = repo_root.name).
#
# Prerequisites: tmux, claude (authenticated), biff, git, uv.
# punt-labs already has channelsEnabled ON; the --dangerously-load flag bypasses
# the plugin allowlist for local server testing.
#
# Usage:
#   bash spikes/channels/harness.sh            # full run
#   bash spikes/channels/harness.sh --check    # preflight only (no claude)
#
set -euo pipefail

SESSION="biff-channels-$$"
STARTUP_TIMEOUT=60
DELIVER_TIMEOUT=30
POLL_INTERVAL=2
PANE_A=0
PANE_B=1
NEEDLE="channel-needle-$(date +%s)"
SERVER_NAME="biff-channels"
ARTIFACT_DIR="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/biff-channels-spike"

BIFF_REPO=""
RECV_DIR=""
SEND_DIR=""
BIFF_USER=""
RESULT="skip"

RED='\033[0;31m'; GREEN='\033[0;32m'; YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
DIM='\033[2m'; BOLD='\033[1m'; RESET='\033[0m'

log()  { echo -e "$*"; }
die()  { echo -e "${RED}$*${RESET}" >&2; exit 1; }

preflight() {
    local missing=()
    command -v tmux   >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing+=(tmux)
    command -v claude >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing+=(claude)
    command -v biff   >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing+=(biff)
    command -v git    >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing+=(git)
    command -v uv     >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing+=(uv)
    if (( ${#missing[@]} > 0 )); then
        die "missing required tools: ${missing[*]}"
    fi
    BIFF_USER=$(gh api user --jq .login 2>/dev/null || whoami)
    log "  ${DIM}user: $BIFF_USER${RESET}"
    log "  ${DIM}claude: $(claude --version 2>/dev/null)${RESET}"
}

setup_repos() {
    BIFF_REPO="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)"
    [ -f "$BIFF_REPO/.biff" ] || die ".biff not found in $BIFF_REPO — run from the biff repo"

    local base
    base=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/biff-channels.XXXXXX")
    RECV_DIR="$base/a/biff"
    SEND_DIR="$base/b/biff"
    mkdir -p "$base/a" "$base/b"
    git clone --quiet "$BIFF_REPO" "$RECV_DIR"
    git clone --quiet "$BIFF_REPO" "$SEND_DIR"
    printf 'enabled = true\n' > "$RECV_DIR/.biff.local"
    printf 'enabled = true\n' > "$SEND_DIR/.biff.local"

    # Register the spike server so `--dangerously-load-development-channels
    # server:biff-channels` resolves it.  BIFF_CHANNELS=1 turns the emitter and
    # capability on for THIS server only.
    cat > "$RECV_DIR/.mcp.json" <<JSON
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "$SERVER_NAME": {
      "command": "uv",
      "args": ["run", "--project", "$BIFF_REPO", "python", "-m", "spikes.channels.serve"],
      "env": { "BIFF_CHANNELS": "1" }
    }
  }
}
JSON
    log "  ${DIM}receiver: $RECV_DIR${RESET}"
    log "  ${DIM}sender:   $SEND_DIR${RESET}"
    log "  ${DIM}server:   $SERVER_NAME → spikes.channels.serve${RESET}"
}

send_slash() {
    local pane=$1; shift
    tmux send-keys -t "$SESSION:0.$pane" -- "$*" Enter
    sleep 1
    tmux send-keys -t "$SESSION:0.$pane" Enter
}

capture_pane() { tmux capture-pane -t "$SESSION:0.$1" -p 2>/dev/null || true; }

wait_for() {
    local pane=$1 pattern=$2 timeout=${3:-$DELIVER_TIMEOUT} elapsed=0
    while (( elapsed < timeout )); do
        if capture_pane "$pane" | grep -qF "$pattern"; then return 0; fi
        sleep "$POLL_INTERVAL"; elapsed=$(( elapsed + POLL_INTERVAL ))
    done
    return 1
}

dump_pane() {
    log "${DIM}--- pane $1 ---${RESET}"
    capture_pane "$1" | grep '.' | tail -20
    log "${DIM}--- end ---${RESET}"
}

setup_tmux() {
    tmux new-session -d -s "$SESSION" -x 220 -y 50 -c "$RECV_DIR"
    tmux split-window -h -t "$SESSION:0" -c "$SEND_DIR"
}

cleanup() {
    log "\n${DIM}cleaning up...${RESET}"
    tmux send-keys -t "$SESSION:0.$PANE_A" C-c 2>/dev/null || true
    tmux send-keys -t "$SESSION:0.$PANE_A" "/exit" Enter 2>/dev/null || true
    sleep 2
    tmux kill-session -t "$SESSION" 2>/dev/null || true
    [ -n "$RECV_DIR" ] && [ -d "$RECV_DIR" ] && rm -rf "$(dirname "$(dirname "$RECV_DIR")")"
}

save_captures() {
    local dir="$ARTIFACT_DIR/captures-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
    mkdir -p "$dir"
    capture_pane $PANE_A > "$dir/pane-A.txt"
    capture_pane $PANE_B > "$dir/pane-B.txt"
    log "${YELLOW}captures: $dir/${RESET}"
}

main() {
    log "${BOLD}Biff Channels spike harness${RESET}\n"

    log "${BOLD}[1/6] Preflight${RESET}"
    preflight
    if [ "${1:-}" = "--check" ]; then
        log "${GREEN}preflight OK — rerun without --check to drive claude${RESET}"
        exit 0
    fi

    log "${BOLD}[2/6] Test repos${RESET}"
    setup_repos

    log "${BOLD}[3/6] tmux${RESET}"
    setup_tmux
    trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM

    log "${BOLD}[4/6] Launch receiver (channels on)${RESET}"
    tmux send-keys -t "$SESSION:0.$PANE_A" \
        "unset CLAUDECODE && claude --dangerously-load-development-channels server:$SERVER_NAME" Enter
    sleep 5
    # New directory → trust prompt; accept it.
    if capture_pane $PANE_A | grep -qF "trust"; then
        tmux send-keys -t "$SESSION:0.$PANE_A" Enter; sleep 2
    fi
    sleep 5
    send_slash $PANE_A "/tty recv"
    if wait_for $PANE_A "recv" "$STARTUP_TIMEOUT"; then
        log "  ${GREEN}receiver ready${RESET}"
    else
        dump_pane $PANE_A; die "receiver did not start"
    fi

    log "${BOLD}[5/6] Trigger arrival via wall${RESET}"
    sleep 3
    tmux send-keys -t "$SESSION:0.$PANE_B" -- "biff wall $NEEDLE" Enter
    log "  ${DIM}sent: biff wall $NEEDLE (sender)${RESET}"
    log "  ${DIM}polling receiver pane for channel render (${DELIVER_TIMEOUT}s)...${RESET}"

    # A rendered channel event shows the needle in the receiver's transcript
    # (Claude reacts to the <channel> tag).  The tool-description path would
    # only surface on the NEXT tool call, so an early hit is channel-driven.
    if wait_for $PANE_A "$NEEDLE" "$DELIVER_TIMEOUT"; then
        RESULT="pass"
        log "  ${GREEN}CHANNEL: PASS — needle rendered in receiver${RESET}"
    else
        RESULT="fail"
        log "  ${RED}CHANNEL: FAIL — needle not rendered${RESET}"
        dump_pane $PANE_A
    fi

    log "${BOLD}[6/6] Result${RESET}"
    case "$RESULT" in
        pass) log "  ${GREEN}PASS${RESET}" ;;
        *)    log "  ${RED}FAIL${RESET}"; save_captures; exit 1 ;;
    esac
}

main "$@"

# Claude Code Channels — feasibility spike findings (biff-qlz)

Mission: `m-2026-07-22-008`. Branch: `spike/channels-harness`. Not for merge.

## Go / No-Go

**GO** on Channels-as-an-additive-emitter. The gating FastMCP question is
settled with observed wire output; dual-support is proven with no regression to
biff's existing delivery. The live latency/coalescing/per-modality *render*
measurements are **operator-pending** — this environment cannot drive an
interactive `claude` session (see §6). Recommendation: **keep** the opt-in
emitter behind the `BIFF_CHANNELS` flag; the one piece not yet in production is
routing the server launch through a channels-aware stdio runner (§4).

## 1. FastMCP verdict — the gate (PASS)

Python FastMCP 3.2.0 (mcp SDK 1.26.0) **can** both (a) advertise
`capabilities.experimental['claude/channel']` and (b) emit a custom
`notifications/claude/channel` over stdio. Two escape hatches are required,
each proven below.

**Escape hatch 1 — capability injection.** `FastMCP.run_stdio_async`
hardcodes `create_initialization_options(notification_options=...)` with **no**
`experimental_capabilities` argument
(`fastmcp/server/mixins/transport.py:216`). To advertise the capability you
must drive the low-level `Server.run` yourself and pass
`experimental_capabilities={"claude/channel": {}}`. FastMCP's
`create_initialization_options` and the SDK's `get_capabilities` both accept and
preserve it.

**Escape hatch 2 — custom-method notification.** `Context.send_notification`
wraps its argument in `mcp.types.ServerNotification` — a closed union whose
members carry `Literal` methods, so it raises `ValidationError` on
`notifications/claude/channel` (verified). The base
`ServerSession.send_notification` performs no union validation — it only calls
`notification.model_dump(...)` and writes the frame — so sending a raw
`Notification[dict, str]` directly on the session rides through untouched.

### Evidence — standalone emitter (`spikes/channels/emitter.py`)

`uv run python -m spikes.channels.gate_probe` captured, over real stdio:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{"experimental":{"claude/channel":{}},"logging":{},"prompts":{"listChanged":false},"resources":{"subscribe":false,"listChanged":false},"tools":{"listChanged":true},"extensions":{"io.modelcontextprotocol/ui":{}}},"serverInfo":{"name":"biff-channels-spike","version":"3.2.0"}}}
{"method":"notifications/claude/channel","params":{"content":"gate-probe-needle","meta":{"source":"biff"}},"jsonrpc":"2.0"}
```

Verdict line: `GATE: PASS`. The capability is advertised in `initialize`, and
the custom notification reaches the wire verbatim with the expected
`params.content` and `params.meta.source`.

### Evidence — real biff server (`spikes/channels/serve.py`)

`BIFF_CHANNELS=1 uv run python -m spikes.channels.gate_probe spikes.channels.serve`
against the **production** biff server (`create_server`, real relay, real
tools) captured:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{...,"capabilities":{"experimental":{"claude/channel":{}},...,"tools":{"listChanged":true},...},"serverInfo":{"name":"biff","version":"3.2.0"},"instructions":"Biff is a communication tool..."}}
```

`serverInfo.name` is `biff` — this is the real server, not the toy. With the
flag **unset**, the same probe shows `"experimental": {}` (no `claude/channel`).
(The probe's own `GATE: FAIL` here is expected and not a defect: it then calls
the toy `emit_channel` tool, which the real server does not have — it correctly
returns `Unknown tool: 'emit_channel'`. The gate assertion of interest is the
`initialize` capability line above.)

## 2. Dual-support — no regression (PROVEN)

The hard constraint: Channels is an opt-in **second** emitter; biff's existing
delivery (tool-description mutation + `tools/list_changed` + status-line file,
DES-004/020/036) must be unchanged when off, and must not double-surface when
on.

**At the wire (real server, §1 evidence):** flag off ⇒ `experimental: {}` and
`tools: {listChanged: true}` exactly as production today; flag on ⇒
`experimental` gains `claude/channel` and nothing else changes. The existing
`tools/list_changed` capability is identical in both.

**At the hook (`tests/test_server/test_channels.py`, 24 tests, all green):**

| Condition | `tools/list_changed` | `claude/channel` |
|---|---|---|
| `BIFF_CHANNELS` unset | sent once | **not** sent |
| `BIFF_CHANNELS=1`, arrival summary present | sent once | sent once |
| `BIFF_CHANNELS=1`, no arrival summary (revert to base) | sent once | **not** sent |

No double-surfacing: the channel carries the *same* summary the tool
description shows, emitted exactly once per arrival (`await_count == 1` for
both paths). A dead session in the channel emit is swallowed (best-effort,
mirroring `notify_tool_list_changed`) so it cannot break the poller.

## 3. Integration — one hook, not a parallel path

The emitter reuses biff's single message-arrival hook,
`notify_tool_list_changed()` in
`src/biff/server/tools/_descriptions.py`. A new keyword `channel_content:
str | None = None` (default `None` ⇒ behavior identical to today) drives the
additive emit on the *same* session — belt path (`ctx.session`) inside a tool
handler, suspenders path (stored `_session`) from the background poller. The
new module `src/biff/server/channels.py` holds the flag check, the capability
map, and the raw-notification emit.

The three message-arrival refreshers pass their arrival summary as
`channel_content`, each gated so only a genuine arrival surfaces:

- `refresh_read_messages` — passes the `"Check messages (N unread)..."` text
  only when `total > 0` (a revert to the base description is not an arrival).
- `refresh_wall` — passes `"[WALL] <text> — <sender>"` only when the wall
  **content key** changed, reusing the same gate vox uses, so a per-~2s
  countdown-timer description tick does **not** re-emit.
- `refresh_talk` — passes the `"[TALK] ..."` text only when the description is
  not the idle base.

## 4. The one production wiring point (not yet done)

`src/biff/__main__.py` launches the server via `server.run(transport="stdio")`
(FastMCP's `run_stdio_async`), which — per escape hatch 1 — does **not** inject
experimental capabilities. So production biff, even with the emitter merged,
would emit the notification but **not advertise the capability**, and Claude
Code would drop the event. `__main__.py` is outside this spike's write-set;
`spikes/channels/serve.py` demonstrates the required launch (drive
`_mcp_server.run` with `experimental_capabilities=channel_experimental_capabilities()`).
Productionizing means routing `mcp_cmd`'s stdio launch through a channels-aware
runner that injects the caps when the flag is on. This is the single remaining
integration edit.

## 5. Latency, coalescing, per-modality

| Question | Method | Result |
|---|---|---|
| FastMCP feasibility (gate) | raw-stdio probe (§1) | **PASS** — observed |
| Capability advertised (real server, on) | probe `serve` with `BIFF_CHANNELS=1` | **PASS** — `experimental.claude/channel` observed |
| Capability absent (real server, off) | probe `serve`, flag unset | **PASS** — `experimental: {}` observed |
| No-regression to `tools/list_changed` | probe both states + 24 unit tests | **PASS** — identical |
| No double-surfacing | unit test `await_count == 1` each | **PASS** — observed |
| Renders + drives model action | inspect live pane for the needle | **OPERATOR-PENDING** (§6) |
| Latency, idle agent | live: `biff wall` → in-pane timestamp | **OPERATOR-PENDING** |
| Latency, busy agent | live: send mid-task | **OPERATOR-PENDING** |
| Coalescing (N rapid sends) | live: count rendered events | **OPERATOR-PENDING** |
| Per-modality render (wall/write/talk) | live: one send each | **OPERATOR-PENDING** (emit decision unit-verified; render pending) |

Design note on coalescing: biff emits per description-change tick (poller
default ~2s), so multiple arrivals within one tick collapse to one refresh and
one channel emit; distinct arrivals across ticks emit per tick. Claude Code's
own turn-boundary channel delivery is the other half of coalescing and can only
be characterized live.

## 6. Why the live measurements are operator-pending

This spike ran as a non-interactive background agent. Three concrete blockers,
none faked around:

1. `claude --help` (version **2.1.206**) does **not** list
   `--dangerously-load-development-channels`. The flag does not error as an
   unknown option, but a `--print` invocation with it produced no output and
   hung (no `biff-channels` server registered in this repo, no TTY) — killed
   after 20s.
2. The environment authenticates via `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, which claude reports
   *disables* claude.ai connectors ("takes precedence over your claude.ai
   login") — this affects plugin/channel loading and is not the interactive
   login path Channels expects.
3. Channels are interactive-TUI-only; a headless/background agent has no pane to
   capture.

## 7. Operator steps to complete the measurements

The harness `spikes/channels/harness.sh` is runnable and preflight-clean
(`bash spikes/channels/harness.sh --check` passes: tmux, claude, biff, git, uv
all present; shellcheck clean). To finish the characterization on an
interactive workstation with a channels-enabled Claude Code login:

1. Confirm the flag name for the installed claude:
   `claude --dangerously-load-development-channels server:biff-channels` starts
   without an "unknown option" error. If the flag was renamed, update
   `SERVER_NAME`/flag in `harness.sh`.
2. Ensure a claude.ai login with `channelsEnabled` (punt-labs has it on); unset
   `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` for the session so the connector/channel path loads.
3. `bash spikes/channels/harness.sh`. It clones biff twice (shared NATS
   namespace), registers `biff-channels` → `spikes.channels.serve` with
   `BIFF_CHANNELS=1` via `.mcp.json`, launches the receiver with the dev-channels
   flag, sends `biff wall <needle>` from the sender pane, and polls the receiver
   pane for the rendered needle.
4. For latency: note the wall-send time vs the needle's appearance; repeat with
   the receiver mid-task for the busy-agent number.
5. For coalescing: send N rapid `biff wall`/`biff write` in a burst; count
   rendered channel events.
6. For per-modality: repeat step 3 substituting `biff write @user:recv <needle>`
   and a talk invite.

## 8. Permission relay for Phase B (biff-6gk) — feasible, one caveat

The same mechanism extends to the optional consent probe.
`notifications/claude/channel/permission` is another custom-method
notification — identical escape hatch, already proven. But
`notifications/claude/channel/permission_request` is a server→client **request**
expecting a response, not a fire-and-forget notification, so it needs the
request path (`session.send_request` with a custom request type) rather than
`send_notification`. That path is **not** exercised by this spike. Verdict:
**likely feasible**, recommend a dedicated follow-up probe that validates a
custom-method request/response round-trip before committing Phase B to it.

## 9. Keep / discard recommendation

**Keep** the emitter: `src/biff/server/channels.py`, the `channel_content`
wiring in `_descriptions.py`, and `tests/test_server/test_channels.py`. It is
additive, off by default, byte-identical to today when off, and covered by 24
tests. **Before any default-on decision**, complete §5's operator-pending
measurements and productionize the §4 capability-advertisement launch. The
`spikes/` tree (emitter, serve, gate_probe, harness) is the reusable
verification kit and can stay on the branch as the characterization record.

## Artifacts

- `spikes/channels/emitter.py` — standalone gate emitter.
- `spikes/channels/gate_probe.py` — raw-stdio probe (`[module]` arg; default
  emitter, pass `spikes.channels.serve` for the real server).
- `spikes/channels/serve.py` — real biff server + capability injection.
- `spikes/channels/harness.sh` — interactive tmux + capture-pane harness.
- `src/biff/server/channels.py` — opt-in emitter (flag, caps, raw emit).
- `src/biff/server/tools/_descriptions.py` — `notify_tool_list_changed`
  `channel_content` wiring + three refreshers.
- `tests/test_server/test_channels.py` — 24 dual-support tests.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# log-session.sh — SessionStart probe for biff-7ak.
#
# Answers the crux question the tty-resume fix hinges on: is Claude Code's
# session_id STABLE across `claude --resume`? SessionStart fires on every
# startup AND resume, with `source` distinguishing them and `session_id` in the
# hook JSON on stdin. This appends one line per session start to
# .tmp/session-probe.log so a resume can be compared to the original startup.
#
# Read the truth: after a /exit + `claude --resume`, look at
# .tmp/session-probe.log — if the `source=resume` line's session_id matches the
# prior `source=startup` line's, the id is stable and Option B is buildable.
#
# Remove: delete the "SessionStart" block from .claude/settings.local.json.
set -euo pipefail

payload="$(cat)"
dir="${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}"
mkdir -p "$dir/.tmp"
python3 - "$payload" "$dir/.tmp/session-probe.log" <<'PY'
import sys, json, datetime
raw, log = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
try:
    d = json.loads(raw or "{}")
except Exception:
    d = {}
line = (
    f'{datetime.datetime.now().isoformat()}  '
    f'source={d.get("source")}  '
    f'session_id={d.get("session_id")}  '
    f'cwd={d.get("cwd")}  '
    f'transcript={d.get("transcript_path")}\n'
)
with open(log, "a") as fh:
    fh.write(line)
PY

tool_input.content:
+1 with a concrete data-loss case from a **stdio** MCP server — so the `Mcp-Session-Id` HTTP-header discussion above doesn't apply to us; we need a **stdio-visible** identifier.

**biff** is a team-communication MCP server. It routes directed messages on a per-session address, `{user}:{tty}`, where `tty` is assigned at server startup. On `claude --resume` the server is a **new process** and re-derives a *different* `tty`, because it has no stable session identity to key on:

- env exposes only `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` (no `CLAUDE_SESSION_ID`);
- the MCP `initialize` `clientInfo` carries only name + version;
- `session_id` is available **only** to the `SessionStart` hook's stdin, never to the server itself.

The result is silent, hard-to-debug message loss and misrouting across a resume:

- **Lost** — a message addressed to the pre-resume `{user}:tty1` lands in an inbox that no live session drains.
- **Misrouted** — `tty` values are recycled, so a *later, different* session can claim the freed number and receive messages meant for the prior occupant.

**Ask:** expose to MCP servers — **stdio included**, via an env var or the `initialize` params — a conversation/run identifier that is **stable across `claude --resume`**; or, failing that, *document* whether the existing `session_id` is guaranteed stable across `--resume`. Either would let the `SessionStart`-hook + shared-PPID correlation (@JoshuaDavid's technique above) deterministically reclaim the prior identity. Today the server cannot know it is the same logical session after a resume, which turns a routing key into a source of lost mail.

  DESIGN-ONLY mission (no code changes) for biff-7ak, a P1 correctness bug: on
  `claude --resume` biff re-derives a NEW tty, causing LOST and MISROUTED
  directed messages, because {user}:{tty} is used as a routing key and ttyN is
  recycled + re-derived per process start. The operator has RATIFIED the fix
  approach (Option B — route on session_id). Your job is to turn that ratified
  shape into (a) a detailed design doc and (b) the precise session-model.tex
  changes to formalize — NOT to implement.

  Read biff-7ak's full notes first: `bd show biff-7ak`. They contain the
  source-confirmed facts you must build on (do not re-derive):
  - session_id IS stable across `claude --resume`/`--continue` and is fresh on
    `--fork-session`/`/branch` (confirmed in ~/Coding/claude-code-main:
    src/cli/print.ts switchSession on non-fork resume; docs/14 §Session
    Ownership). Fork getting a fresh id => a fresh tty is CORRECT.
  - The MCP server gets NO session identity directly (env=CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR
    only; initialize clientInfo=name+version only; session_id is SessionStart-
    hook-only). The bridge is the shared PPID: the SessionStart hook and the
    MCP server are both children of the same `claude` process; biff already has
    a process-tree walk (find_session_key, DES-011) and a hint-file idiom
    (hook.py/markers.py).
  - The resume picker hides the currently-active session, so a resumed session
    has already exited => its tty reservation is free/reclaimable.

  RATIFIED design (operator-confirmed) to detail and formalize:
  1. Durable session identity = Claude Code session_id. ttyN demotes to a
     human-facing DISPLAY ALIAS, not the routing key.
  2. Plumbing: SessionStart hook captures session_id (stdin) and writes it keyed
     by the claude PID (its PPID); the MCP server reads it at startup via its
     own process-tree walk to the same claude PID. Favorable ordering
     (SessionStart fires before the server connects); server retries if absent.
  3. Delivery re-keys the durable inbox from tty to session_id
     (biff.{repo}.inbox.{user}.{session_id}, replacing the DES-016 tty-keyed
     subject). A KV binding session_id <-> ttyN exists only for display and
     address resolution. `write user:tty1` resolves tty1 -> current session_id
     AT SEND TIME and delivers to that id's inbox. Messages are ephemeral/POP,
     no history (DES-006) => clean cutover, no migration.
  4. Normal resume reuses session_id => reclaims its ttyN + same inbox (no loss,
     no misroute). Fork => new session_id => new tty (correct).

  Note the addressing SYNTAX change is tracked separately as biff-5gb (drop the
  @ prefix: user:ttyN not @user:ttyN). Design your address-resolution surface so
  biff-5gb folds into the same edits; do not implement biff-5gb here, but do not
  design anything that conflicts with bare-user:tty addressing.

  - "The precise session-model.tex changes SPECIFIED for jms to formalize in the implementation phase: the new/changed state (identity = session_id; session_id<->tty binding), the resume-reclaim transition, the fork-fresh transition, and the delivery invariant (a directed message is delivered to the addressed session's session_id-keyed inbox; a resumed session loses nothing; a recycled ttyN never delivers to a stale inbox). Describe them precisely; do NOT edit the .tex in this mission."

  - "No code changes and no .tex edits — design + spec-change specification only. Cite file:line for every claim about current behavior."
